title: The World’s Largest Marine Turtle Makes a Move South - Nautilus
gist: A Chelonian Conservation and Biology study finds warming oceans are pushing critically endangered eastern Pacific leatherback turtles to nest about 1,000 miles south in Ecuador rather than Mexico and Costa Rica.

insights.claim: Warming oceans are shifting critically endangered eastern Pacific leatherback sea turtles (Dermochelys coriacea) from their typical nesting along the west coasts of Mexico and Costa Rica to beaches about 1,000 miles south in Ecuador, per a study in Chelonian Conservation and Biology.
insights.so_what: Range shifts relocate conservation priorities (and ecotourism) southward.
insights.quote: they’re showing up about 1,000 miles south in Ecuador
insights.locator: A recent study in the journal
insights.speaker: Devin Reese

insights.claim: Leatherbacks tolerate waters from 32°F up to 86°F using cool upwellings, activity-generated heat and insulating fat, yet ocean warming still exceeds their limits for nesting.
insights.so_what: Even thermally tolerant species are being displaced by warming.
insights.speaker: Devin Reese
